title: slice-reserve-latency-aware-allocator-and-kernel-hinting
creator: Leila Thompson
description: Goal: Implement a latency-reservation micro-slice allocator that cooperates with kernel-selection hints so latency-sensitive requests get small reserved execution windows, while opportunistic throughput requests can be packed into larger slices. This ticket prototypes the allocator, integrates attention-sparsity signals for kernel hinting, and produces A/B perf data to validate fairness and cost trade-offs. Motivation: current phase-splitting policies reduce tail latency for single-tenant bursts but struggle when mixed latency/throughput workloads share GPUs. We want a low-complexity allocator that: 1) preserves p95/p99 for latency SLA tenants by reserving small micro-slices and fast kernels, 2) allows opportunistic consolidation to improve throughput and GPU utilization, and 3) exposes knobs to trade latency vs cost per-tenant.
acceptance_criteria: Latency tenants: p95 end-to-end gen latency <= baseline p95 * 1.08 in mixed workloads (with <=10% throughput load)
Throughput consolidation: overall tokens/sec for best-effort tenants increases >= 10% vs conservative allocator under high load scenarios
Fairness: tenant credit depletion prevents starvation for lower-priority tenants in < 60s under steady-state load
Kernel hinting: allocator emits kernel preference tag to runtime and runtime honors kernel hint >= 90% of cases when affinities match
Smoke tests and regression suites added; CI perf benchmarks included
Design doc and rollout runbook reviewed and approved by runtime/infra leads
work_items: Design: finalize micro-slice reservation model and token-credit algorithm
Implementation: allocator core with tenant slot reservation and opportunistic filler loop
Integration: wire allocator kernel-hint metadata into request envelope
Runtime: kernel-selector read kernel-hint and attempt to schedule matching kernel; fallback path metrics
Tests: unit tests for credit draining, integration perf runs with mixed workload harness
Metrics: add histograms for reserved-slice usage, hint-hit-rate, tenant-starvation-duration
Canary: deploy to canary pool with two tenants (latency SLA + high throughput)
updates: 2026-02-11: Design kickoff with runtime and model-kernel teams. Agreed to keep reservation logic external to kernel selector to minimize cross-component coupling.
2026-02-20: Prototype allocator implemented (branch: feat/slice-reserve). Microbench harness created to simulate short-chat (latency) vs long-generate (throughput) tenants.

2026-02-25: Early perf run: p95 improved by ~14% for latency tenant, but opportunistic throughput fell 6% when reservation was too aggressive. Decided to add adaptive reservation decay based on observed util.
2026-03-02: Added attention-sparsity signal extraction in prefill stage; allocator now tags requests with 'kernel_hint: sparse_fast' for models with >40% zeroed attention rows in probe window.
2026-03-08: PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1229 (allocator + hint plumbing). Requesting runtime owner review.
2026-03-10: Design review feedback from Maya (infra): caution on multi-tenant memory accounting when reserving KV cache slots. Action: add per-tenant cache cap check before reservation completes.
2026-03-12: Integration test failures isolated to kernel fallback path (hint not respected when kernel probe times out). Added timeout to hint path and metric 'hint_probe_latency_ms'.
